s: Images, containers, Dockerfile, Compose, volumes, networking
d: Docker packages your app with its entire environment — solving 'works on my machine' forever. Containers are lightweight, reproducible, and the foundation of modern deployment. Every backend dev must know Docker.

p: Docker packages an application and all its dependencies (OS libs, runtime, code) into a standardized unit called a Container. Containers run exactly the same way on any machine.
1. Write a Dockerfile (instructions to build image).
2. `docker build` to create an Image (read-only template).
3. `docker run` to start a Container (running instance of image).
4. Docker Compose manages multi-container apps (e.g., App + DB).

FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json .
RUN npm install
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["npm", "start"]

Virtual Machine vs Container:
[App A]   [App B]      [App A]   [App B]
[GuestOS] [GuestOS]    [--- Bins/Libs ---]
[ Hypervisor    ]      [ Docker Engine   ]
[ Host OS       ]      [ Host OS         ]
VMs are heavy. Containers share Host OS and are lightweight.
